Threat scenario: Forged or modified inter-agent message impersonates a trusted agent or fabricates findings.
Architectural control: Verify detached signature against trusted key registry; bind all identity and routing fields into protected preimage.
Trust boundary: Agent process to A2A ingress; A2A verifier to key registry
Required implementation change: Implement versioned envelope; trusted key-to-AgentId/MissionId binding; recipient and mission comparison; fixed Ed25519; key revocation and rotation.
Required security test and test ID: Existing pending TEST-A2A-FORGERY-001 expanded; proposed TEST-A2A-REVOKED-KEY-001
Expected result / failure behavior: Reject invalid signature, unknown/revoked key, altered protected field, invalid key domain, or identity mismatch before dispatch.
Required evidence artifact: Test report, vector-set hash, commit SHA, CI run ID, signature verification logs with payload omitted
Human approval dependency: Human approval of ADR-005, key domain, and key custody

Threat scenario: Captured signed A2A message is replayed after acceptance or after restart.
Architectural control: Durable unique replay ledger keyed by mission/sender/recipient/key/nonce; atomic inbox reservation; transactional dispatch recovery.
Trust boundary: A2A ingress to durable storage and agent inbox
Required implementation change: Persist acceptance across restart; concurrent insert has one winner; use outbox/idempotency; Bloom filter cannot decide acceptance.
Required security test and test ID: Proposed TEST-A2A-REPLAY-001; existing TEST-REPLAY-001 applies only to action proposal replay
Expected result / failure behavior: First valid delivery may be accepted once; duplicates deny; storage failure denies and no dispatch occurs.
Required evidence artifact: Concurrency run artifact, restart recovery artifact, DB schema/hash, CI run ID
Human approval dependency: Human approval of replay retention and inbox/outbox lifecycle

Threat scenario: Valid message from mission A is replayed or routed into mission B.
Architectural control: Derive active mission from authenticated context; compare signed mission to receiver/task; key and inbox records are mission-scoped.
Trust boundary: A2A sender/receiver and mission store boundary
Required implementation change: Bind mission to trusted token/key registry and signed preimage; do not authorize from header claim alone.
Required security test and test ID: Proposed TEST-A2A-MISSION-001; TEST-MISSION-ISOLATION-001 is adjacent DB coverage only
Expected result / failure behavior: Reject cross-mission message with sanitized denial; do not disclose mission existence; no inbox write or dispatch.
Required evidence artifact: Cross-mission negative test, audit event hash, CI run ID
Human approval dependency: Human approval of mission-bound key registry contract

Threat scenario: A signed message is delivered to a different agent, broadcast group, or unintended task.
Architectural control: Sign recipient/audience and parent task; receiver compares to its local authenticated identity; fan-out requires explicit policy.
Trust boundary: A2A transport and receiving agent boundary
Required implementation change: Define direct-recipient only for v1 or separately authorize group addressing; reject missing, wildcard, or mismatched recipient.
Expected result / failure behavior: Reject wrong recipient before agent context; no implicit broadcast.
Required evidence artifact: Recipient-mismatch vector and CI result
Human approval dependency: Human approval of direct-recipient vs fan-out behavior

Threat scenario: Compromised agent uses signer as an oracle to sign arbitrary identity, delegation, approval, or action claims.
Architectural control: Signing service constructs protected fields from kernel-issued active context and allowlisted message schemas; separate AGENT-MESSAGE-SIGNING key domain.
Trust boundary: Untrusted agent to signing service; signer to key store
Required implementation change: No arbitrary-byte API; no direct key possession; bind subject/mission/task/recipient; rate-limit; deny action authorization and scope-changing message types.
Expected result / failure behavior: Reject arbitrary bytes, capability tokens, approval claims, widened delegation, unknown types, expired context, and caller-supplied identity overrides.
Required evidence artifact: Signer policy test artifact, key-domain audit, CI run ID
Human approval dependency: Human approval of key domain, signer owner, allowed message types

Threat scenario: Malformed, duplicate-key, trailing, unknown-field, or wrong-version message exploits parser differentials.
Architectural control: UTF-8 strict JSON; 65,536-byte cap; depth 8; reject duplicate keys, trailing content, unknown fields, invalid types, and unsupported version at each ingress.
Trust boundary: Wire ingress to Rust/Python parser and typed envelope
Owning component: Rust A2A ingress / Python transport adapter
Required implementation change: Reuse Rust StrictJsonParser only where actually called; Python parser must independently match exact behavior; call end-of-input check; no permissive fallback.
Expected result / failure behavior: Reject before authorization or dispatch on any parser ambiguity; sanitize error; do not partially construct message.
Required evidence artifact: Shared malformed corpus, parser test output, CI run ID
Human approval dependency: Human approval of protocol/parser versioning; current parser source gap must be fixed

Threat scenario: Deep nesting, large arrays, oversized messages, slow input, or signature floods exhaust CPU/memory/threads.
Architectural control: Apply byte/depth/item-count/time/concurrency limits before expensive parsing and crypto; per-agent and per-mission quotas.
Trust boundary: A2A ingress resource boundary
Required implementation change: Define item-count and crypto rate budgets in addition to existing 64 KiB/depth 8; bounded reads and cancellation.
Expected result / failure behavior: Reject over-budget requests early; process remains available; limiter/storage failure denies.
Required evidence artifact: Fuzz corpus, memory/CPU traces, adversarial CI artifact
Human approval dependency: Human approval of budgets and denial thresholds

Requirement / Invariant / Threat ID: TRD §7; INV-005, INV-006; CTRL-TOCTOU-BINDING-001; RFC8785 proposal
Threat scenario: Different canonical bytes across runtimes produce signature/hash disagreement or parameter mutation bypass.
Architectural control: Single ratified canonicalization standard and identical Rust/Python parsed-value rules; domain-separated payload/action hashes.
Trust boundary: Rust and Python normalization/signature boundary
Required implementation change: Ratify JCS or alternative; replace or prove current Rust routine; add Python implementation and shared official/ARKA vectors; version hash migration.
Expected result / failure behavior: Any mismatch or unsupported number/Unicode input denies; approval hash remains bound to exact canonical action.
Required evidence artifact: Official vector results, 100+ shared vectors, hash/signature preimage artifact, independent review
Human approval dependency: Human approval of canonicalization standard and stored-hash migration

Threat scenario: Native LLM tool call bypasses normalization or supplies trusted capability, identity, risk, scope, or approval fields.
Architectural control: Tool adapter maps only registered names to typed capability proposals; kernel derives identity/risk/scope and makes authorization decision.
Trust boundary: LLM output to agent adapter to Rust kernel
Required implementation change: Implement one raw proposal ingress; prevent direct SDK/worker/broker dispatch; make trusted context kernel-derived; reject unknown tools and fields.
Expected result / failure behavior: Policy DENY cannot dispatch; unknown tool or spoofed field rejects before authorization.
Required evidence artifact: Call-graph review, negative integration test, CI run ID
Human approval dependency: Human approval of tool-to-capability registry ownership

Threat scenario: Caller constructs/deserializes a CanonicalAction and calls Broker without kernel authorization.
Architectural control: Require unforgeable mission-bound expiring single-use kernel receipt or durable authorized-state lookup; broker verifies action and parameter hashes.
Trust boundary: Kernel to Execution Broker trust boundary
Required implementation change: Broker must validate proof of exact authorized state and recompute/bind action data; make raw CanonicalAction insufficient.
Required security test and test ID: Proposed TEST-BROKER-FORGED-ACTION-001; existing TEST-PARAM-MUTATION-001 is adjacent only
Expected result / failure behavior: Forged, expired, mismatched, replayed, or altered action is denied before side effects; proof lookup/storage failure denies.
Required evidence artifact: Broker ingress negative test, authorization receipt spec, CI and audit artifacts
Human approval dependency: Human approval of receipt vs durable-state contract

Threat scenario: Unknown or wrong-typed tool parameters reach execution because parameter object is arbitrary JSON.
Architectural control: CapabilityRegistry owns a versioned parameter schema; strict deny-unknown and type/range validation before authorization.
Trust boundary: Raw proposal to ActionNormalizer
Required implementation change: Add per-capability parameter schemas and validate nested values; do not treat envelope deny_unknown_fields as payload schema validation.
Expected result / failure behavior: Unknown parameter, missing required field, wrong type, invalid range, or schema lookup failure denies.
Required evidence artifact: Schema fixtures, negative test results, schema/version hash
Human approval dependency: Human approval of capability schema ownership/versioning

Requirement / Invariant / Threat ID: PRD §17.2; TRD §30; INV-001, INV-007; THREAT-PROMPT-INJECTION; CTRL-PROMPT-GUARD-001
Threat scenario: Target content or retrieved text instructs LLM to reveal secrets, alter scope, or bypass controls.
Architectural control: Treat all target/retrieved/model content as untrusted; delimit/quarantine as defense-in-depth; kernel policy does not consume prompt authority.
Trust boundary: Evidence/retrieval to prompt context; model output to action adapter
Required implementation change: Implement provenance-preserving quarantine and deterministic schema/authority separation; no prompt-only security claim.
Expected result / failure behavior: Injected instructions cannot alter policy or dispatch; uncertain classification denies external use.
Required evidence artifact: Adversarial prompt corpus, context assembly trace, denial test artifact
Human approval dependency: Human approval of external-data policy and prompt control criteria

Threat scenario: Compromised agent reads provider API key from env, files, /proc, shared memory, logs, or errors.
Architectural control: Separate OS identity/process; gateway-only secret resolver; no shared UID/address space; redacted errors and logs.
Trust boundary: Agent process to Gateway process and credential store
Owning component: LLM Gateway / service manager / secret provider
Required implementation change: Implement OS isolation and test /proc, ptrace, filesystem, environment inheritance, crash/error/log paths using synthetic key values.
Expected result / failure behavior: Agent cannot read or retrieve secret; provider secret never enters model, evidence, memory, audit, or agent output.
Required evidence artifact: OS-level test artifact, synthetic-secret scan report, CI run ID
Human approval dependency: Human approval of topology and credential source; no real-secret co-location exception

Threat scenario: Secret, credential, token, confidential evidence, or unnecessary PII is sent to provider.
Architectural control: Deterministic source classification; typed allowlisted context; minimization; redaction; policy per provider; pattern scan only defense-in-depth.
Trust boundary: Evidence store to Gateway request to external provider
Owning component: Evidence classifier / context builder / Gateway policy
Required implementation change: Block secrets and credentials always; default external policy to public-only; require operator policy for internal/confidential; deny unknown labels.
Expected result / failure behavior: Forbidden or unclassified content aborts before socket write; policy/filter error denies; no fallback.
Required evidence artifact: Classified fixture corpus, serialized request capture with fake secrets, CI run ID
Human approval dependency: Human approval of provider-specific sensitivity classes

Threat scenario: Agent bypasses gateway and exfiltrates prompt data directly through arbitrary socket or ambient proxy.
Architectural control: OS/network-layer deny for agent egress; allow only kernel/gateway IPC; explicit Gateway provider allowlist; ignore ambient proxy variables.
Trust boundary: Agent OS network namespace/firewall to external network
Required implementation change: Implement OS egress controls and verify HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY, raw TCP, IPv4/IPv6, subprocess and DNS paths cannot bypass.
Expected result / failure behavior: Direct egress and proxy bypass are physically denied; failure to install policy prevents agent startup.
Required evidence artifact: Namespace/firewall policy artifact and real OS denial test
Human approval dependency: Human approval of deployment/network topology

Threat scenario: Provider hostname resolves to private or unsafe address, mixed answer, or changes between validation and connect.
Architectural control: Resolve immediately before each connection; validate every A/AAAA address; default-deny unsafe ranges; pin exact IP; compare peer; use configured host for TLS verification.
Trust boundary: Gateway to DNS and pinned provider socket
Required implementation change: Reuse network policy only if its address classes meet provider policy; add provider hostname allowlist and connection-time policy.
Expected result / failure behavior: Any unsafe/mixed/out-of-allowlist answer, resolution failure, peer mismatch, or revalidation failure denies.
Required evidence artifact: DNS adversarial test results, resolved-address policy trace, socket peer and TLS test artifact
Human approval dependency: Human approval of provider host allowlist and local endpoint exceptions

Threat scenario: Provider redirect reaches unapproved host, private/loopback/link-local/cloud metadata address, IPv6 bypass, or downgrades to HTTP.
Architectural control: Disable redirects by default; if allowed, revalidate target host, DNS, IP, scope, TLS hostname and hop count for every hop; block metadata and unsafe ranges.
Trust boundary: Gateway provider HTTP client to redirected destination
Required implementation change: Add provider-specific redirect and endpoint rules; no loopback/private exception without explicit local-model profile; block all metadata ranges.
Required security test and test ID: Existing TEST-REDIRECT-001; TEST-METADATA-001; TEST-IPV6-BYPASS-001; proposed TEST-LLM-REDIRECT-001
Expected result / failure behavior: Reject redirect to non-allowlisted, private, metadata, unsafe IPv6, or downgraded destination.
Required evidence artifact: Redirect matrix and metadata/IPv6 adversarial test output
Human approval dependency: Human approval of redirect and local-model policies

Threat scenario: Hostile stdout/stderr or model tool output injects control codes or instructions into evidence/prompt.
Architectural control: Treat all tool output as untrusted; preserve raw hash and provenance; sanitize for display/context; do not trust delimiters from input.
Trust boundary: Worker output to evidence store and agent context
Required implementation change: Implement deterministic normalization and storage/display separation; no lossy overwrite of evidence source.
Expected result / failure behavior: Escape/control code handling is deterministic; output cannot change policy or execute; sanitizer failure quarantines data.
Required evidence artifact: Raw and sanitized artifact hashes, adversarial output CI report
Human approval dependency: Human approval of evidence retention/sanitization policy

Threat scenario: Recursive or malformed HTML/XML/JSON/PDF input exhausts resources or escapes parser boundary.
Architectural control: Parse hostile artifacts in bounded unprivileged process; byte/depth/time/memory caps; provenance and classification before persistence/egress.
Trust boundary: Raw target artifact to evidence parser and store
Required implementation change: Implement actual OS sandbox, parser quotas, safe crash recovery, and classification; do not rely only on stripping ANSI or prompt wrappers.
Expected result / failure behavior: Malformed input rejects/quarantines without kernel/host escape; no unclassified evidence persists or reaches LLM.
Required evidence artifact: OS sandbox test, malformed corpus hash, resource trace, CI run ID
Human approval dependency: Human approval of parser isolation profile

Threat scenario: Poisoned graph or retrieval assertion influences scope or authorization without trustworthy evidence.
Architectural control: Bind assertions to immutable evidence hashes, source/trust/sensitivity; graph is advisory and kernel never grants authority from graph state.
Trust boundary: Evidence store and knowledge graph to agent planning/kernel
Required implementation change: Implement evidence pointer validation and trust labels; specify vector-store isolation if selected; keep graph out of authority path.
Expected result / failure behavior: Unsupported or cross-mission assertion is quarantined and cannot affect kernel authorization.
Required evidence artifact: Graph provenance test, evidence hash verification report, CI run ID
Human approval dependency: Human approval of graph/vector-store architecture

Threat scenario: Compromised model/plugin/dependency, poisoned embedding, or misinformation causes unsafe reasoning.
Architectural control: Track model/provider provenance and dependencies; preserve source evidence and uncertainty; retrieval isolation and update provenance.
Trust boundary: Build pipeline, provider/model adapter, retrieval/evidence boundary
Required implementation change: Define model/runtime/plugin inventory, provenance/hash/licensing/update policy and retrieval tenant boundaries; existing broad dependency scan is not complete LLM coverage.
Required security test and test ID: Existing TEST-SUPPLY-CHAIN-001 is general; proposed TEST-LLM-MODEL-PROVENANCE-001 and TEST-VECTOR-TENANT-ISOLATION-001
Expected result / failure behavior: Unverified model/plugin/embedding or unsupported claim cannot be treated as trusted evidence; supply-chain failure blocks release.
Required evidence artifact: SBOM/model manifest, signed provenance, retrieval-isolation tests, CI run ID
Human approval dependency: Human approval of supported models, plugins, and vector-store scope

Threat scenario: Agent loop, retries, concurrency, token use, or provider spend exceeds mission/operator budget.
Architectural control: Kernel-owned proposal/rate budget; Gateway-owned inference/token/cost caps; worker OS quotas; no agent-adjustable limits.
Trust boundary: Agent orchestrator, Gateway, kernel governor, worker OS
Required implementation change: Add provider-token/cost/request limits, retry/backoff caps, recursion/concurrency ceilings, per-mission metering, and deny on state loss.
Required security test and test ID: Existing TEST-RESOURCE-001 and TEST-WORKER-RESOURCE-001; proposed TEST-LLM-BUDGET-001
Expected result / failure behavior: Excess budget stops new requests/dispatch; unknown counter state denies; no unbounded retry.
Required evidence artifact: Budget adversarial test, provider usage record, OS cgroup evidence, CI artifact
Human approval dependency: Human approval of maximum cost, concurrency, retry, and token budgets

Threat scenario: Completed or expired ActionProposal is resubmitted.
Architectural control: SQLite transaction and unique replay key in kernel; action replay is distinct from proposed A2A replay.
Trust boundary: Kernel authorization transaction/storage
Required implementation change: Retain existing unique replay enforcement; add mapping only for A2A separately.
Expected result / failure behavior: Second action authorization is DENY; DB/storage errors deny and transaction rolls back.
Required evidence artifact: Existing checkpoint P1-D test artifact and CI record
Human approval dependency: No new architecture decision; preserve existing key format unless approved

Threat scenario: Kernel, DB, parser, policy, approval, audit, or emergency-stop state errors and fallback paths.
Architectural control: Fail-closed decision logic; no alternate parser/network/credential/execution path; sanitized external errors.
Trust boundary: Every trusted control boundary
Required implementation change: Extend existing kernel fail-closed contract to new Phase 3 services and ensure sanitized reason codes without sensitive context.
Expected result / failure behavior: Any missing or inconsistent control state denies; no fallback side effect; no sensitive internal detail exposed.
Required evidence artifact: Fault-injection report, sanitized error assertions, CI run ID
Human approval dependency: Human approval of external error categories and release criteria

Threat scenario: Agent fabricates capability or expands target scope based on discovery.
Architectural control: Kernel token, capability registry, scope evaluator, target validation, and approval remain authoritative.
Trust boundary: Agent proposal to kernel policy and network connection
Required implementation change: Ensure any new Phase3 adapter supplies no authority fields; retain connection-time scope checks.
Expected result / failure behavior: Forged capability and out-of-scope target deny before broker dispatch.
Required evidence artifact: Existing P1 scope/signature tests and CI records
Human approval dependency: No new authority; preserve current kernel invariants

Threat scenario: Phase completion status and per-threat traceability disagree, obscuring what is implemented vs pending.
Architectural control: Maintain bidirectional status and evidence links; validator must check lifecycle consistency, not only referential integrity.
Trust boundary: Security model registries and release workflow
Required implementation change: Reconcile Phase2 rows with null targets and PENDING status; add validator assertion for phase-status/test/traceability consistency through approved baseline changes.
Required security test and test ID: Existing TEST-P0-TRACEABILITY-001 currently checks refs; proposed TEST-PHASE-STATUS-CONSISTENCY-001
Expected result / failure behavior: Report inconsistent status as CI failure; do not infer phase acceptance from the 100% reference count.
Required evidence artifact: Validator output, reconciled registry diff, baseline manifest update after approval
Human approval dependency: Human approval required before modifying security baselines

Threat scenario: Prompt injection through target content or retrieval.
Architectural control: Quarantine, provenance, authority separation; kernel authorization independent of prompt.
Trust boundary: Evidence to model and model to action boundary
Required implementation change: Implement and test direct/indirect payload coverage; prompt template alone is insufficient.
Expected result / failure behavior: No policy override, authorization, or direct execution; fail closed on uncertain content.
Required evidence artifact: Adversarial corpus, decision trace, CI artifact
Human approval dependency: Human approval of acceptance criteria

Threat scenario: Sensitive information or system prompt material is elicited or sent externally.
Architectural control: Secret isolation and deterministic egress policy; prompt secrecy is not a control.
Trust boundary: Agent/Gateway/provider boundary
Required implementation change: Use process isolation, sensitivity labels, context minimization, exact destination policy, and secret scan as layered defense.
Expected result / failure behavior: Secret-bearing request is blocked before network send; no credentials returned in provider errors.
Required evidence artifact: Synthetic-secret scans and provider request fixture
Human approval dependency: Human approval of provider-specific data classes

Threat scenario: Compromised library, model artifact, plugin, or provider adapter.
Architectural control: Existing dependency scanning is a baseline, not complete model/plugin provenance.
Trust boundary: Build/runtime supply chain
Required implementation change: Define model/plugin SBOM, hashes, signatures, licenses, update/revocation policy and origin.
Required security test and test ID: TEST-SUPPLY-CHAIN-001 exists for broad dependencies; proposed TEST-LLM-MODEL-PROVENANCE-001
Expected result / failure behavior: Unverified artifacts blocked from release; dependency scan pass alone does not close model provenance risk.
Required evidence artifact: SBOM, model artifact manifest and provenance attestations
Human approval dependency: Human approval of model/plugin sources

Threat scenario: Poisoned retrieval, embedding or graph assertion biases agent analysis.
Architectural control: Evidence hash provenance and tenant/mission boundaries; retrieved facts remain non-authoritative.
Trust boundary: Evidence/retrieval to planning
Required implementation change: Threat-model vector/embedding implementation if selected; enforce evidence pointers and source validation.
Required security test and test ID: TEST-GRAPHIFY-POISONING-001 pending; TEST-RAG-POISONING-001 pending; proposed TEST-VECTOR-TENANT-ISOLATION-001
Expected result / failure behavior: Unsupported or cross-mission evidence cannot influence authority; no vector store is assumed implemented.
Required evidence artifact: Poisoning corpus, retrieval provenance, tenant-isolation result
Human approval dependency: Human approval of graph/vector product and scope

Threat scenario: Improperly handled tool/model output causes injection, corruption, or parser compromise.
Architectural control: Typed output handling, sanitization, resource limits, isolated parser; retain raw evidence hash.
Trust boundary: Worker/model output to evidence/UI/parser
Required implementation change: Implement sandbox and escape handling; do not equate sanitization with trust.
Expected result / failure behavior: Malformed output quarantined; parser/resource failure cannot affect kernel or accept unclassified evidence.
Required evidence artifact: Raw/sanitized hashes, parser sandbox CI result
Human approval dependency: Human approval of parser profile and evidence policy

Threat scenario: Excessive agency or child task escalation.
Architectural control: Monotonic delegation and kernel-owned scope/capabilities/budget/approval.
Trust boundary: Orchestrator delegation to child and kernel auth
Required implementation change: Preserve child subset checks; no message or model can delegate authority absent kernel token.
Required security test and test ID: TEST-RESOURCE-001 and TEST-CAPABILITY-SCOPE-001 existing; proposed TEST-CHILD-MONOTONICITY-001 for all dimensions
Expected result / failure behavior: Widened child bounds deny; no dispatch.
Required evidence artifact: Delegation matrix and negative tests
Human approval dependency: Human approval for role/capability matrix

Threat scenario: Model-generated misinformation is mistaken for observed evidence or changes scope.
Architectural control: Separate observation, inference, source confidence, and evidence hash; model statements cannot modify policy.
Trust boundary: Model output to evidence/knowledge graph
Required implementation change: Store provenance and uncertainty labels; prevent model-created graph claims from becoming authorized targets.
Expected result / failure behavior: Unverified claim is labeled and cannot authorize action; report retains evidence references.
Required evidence artifact: Provenance test output and sample report record
Human approval dependency: Human approval of reporting confidence semantics

Requirement / Invariant / Threat ID: OWASP LLM10; PRD §§17–18; TRD §32; THREAT-RESOURCE-EXHAUSTION; THREAT-BUDGET-OVERRUN
Threat scenario: Runaway agent loop, retry storm, oversized context, or provider cost spike.
Architectural control: Kernel recursion/proposal budgets plus Gateway request/token/concurrency/cost ceilings.
Trust boundary: Agent loop, Gateway, kernel governor
Required implementation change: Add provider cost and token telemetry with hard limits; counters are trusted persistent state and cannot be agent modified.
Expected result / failure behavior: Budget exhaustion denies new requests and dispatches; no retry loop on unknown state.
Required evidence artifact: Usage/budget test artifact and provider logs with secrets redacted
Human approval dependency: Human approval of spend and throughput ceilings
